detail.title: Synthesis of Foundational Assumption Testing and Metareasoning Disconnects in LLMs
detail.summary: This cycle generates synthesis notebooks for foundational assumption testing in reasoning systems and the detection of metareasoning gaps in large language models. The research connects formal logical limits with the operational reality of reasoning-answer gaps in transformer models.

children.title: Foundational Limitations in Axiomatic Reasoning and LLM CoT

detail.title: Foundational Limitations in Axiomatic Reasoning and LLM CoT
detail.summary: This synthesis connects Gödelian incompleteness, which posits that formal systems cannot prove their own consistency, with the emerging research on how Large Language Models generate reasoning traces. While mathematical logic defines structural limits, modern Chain-of-Thought research focuses on the sensitivity of models to prompt stimuli and their inherent reasoning-answer gaps.
detail.reason: The project requires synthesizing the formal logical background (Gödel) with the operational evidence regarding CoT sensitivity to determine if foundational assumptions can be tested within the model's own reasoning trace.

detail.title: Detecting and Aligning Metareasoning Disconnects
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the 'reasoning-answer hit gap' in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). It details how alignment frameworks like MR-ALIGN can quantify state-transition probabilities within the thinking process to improve factual fidelity without external verifiers.
detail.reason: This action synthesizes evidence regarding the model's ability to detect its own reasoning failures through internal probability shifts.
